assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theory-led discovery that opened a new class of tunable flat-band quantum matter. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle from band-structure reasoning, and the correlated-insulator and superconducting phases seen in twisted bilayer graphene have since spread across moire materials. Originality and breadth are high, and the electronic-structure content is the kind of calculation-meets-experiment story I find most convincing.
assessment.attribution: The prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald) and the first experimental demonstrations (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators) are cleanly identifiable and fit a three-person configuration. Other contributors, such as early moire band-structure work and independent experimental groups, are not in the supplied credit, so a small part of the credit landscape is left unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the correlated and superconducting states, and the continuum-model picture has been tested repeatedly. Recognition is timely. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated, but the discovery of the flat-band platform does not depend on that.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism for superconductivity in magic-angle graphene is not settled.
I am relying on my own recollection of the historical record rather than anything verified here.
Whether the prize is better framed on the theory prediction or on the experimental discovery of the correlated phases.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the later giant TMR in MgO barriers turned spin-dependent tunnelling into the read-head and MRAM technology that followed the giant magnetoresistance prize. The physics of coherent, symmetry-selective tunnelling through crystalline barriers was predicted from first-principles calculations before it was measured, which makes the story close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki established room-temperature TMR in 1995. Parkin is credited for the MgO giant TMR and its engineering. The MgO result was reached in parallel by other groups (notably Yuasa and colleagues) who are not in the supplied credit, so the credit supports a fair configuration but leaves the MgO part partly unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation and large-scale technological use. This is mature and arguably overdue relative to the 2007 GMR prize.
uncertainties: Credit for the MgO coherent-tunnelling result is shared with people outside the supplied names.
The discovery is a compound of room-temperature TMR and MgO TMR, and the parts may deserve different recognition.
Details of priority are from memory and not independently checked.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the standard non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons and is combined with density functional theory for real materials. It explains the Mott transition, and heavy-fermion and transition-metal oxide spectra. Its lasting impact on computational materials theory is very large. I know the method well in practice, so I weigh both its power and its limits (local self-energy, cluster extensions).
assessment.attribution: Vollhardt, with Metzner, introduced the infinite-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar built the mapping to an impurity problem; Kotliar led the DFT combination. Metzner, Müller-Hartmann and others who made decisive contributions are not in the supplied credit, so the three-person configuration leaves out real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Developed over three decades with extensive use and cross-validation against experiment. The theory is secure, though a prize for a method rather than a single discovery is less clean.
uncertainties: Prizes for theoretical methods are less often awarded than for a specific physical discovery.
Credit omits Metzner and Müller-Hartmann, which is a substantive attribution gap.
Quantitative predictive accuracy for real materials remains uneven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators changed how band structure is classified, with robust edge or surface transport protected by symmetry. The quantum spin Hall prediction and the HgTe observation are a clear theory-to-experiment chain, and material-specific band calculations were part of the proposals. The impact on condensed matter is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele, who is not in this entry's credit) provided the central theory, and Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe wells. Xue is credited here mainly for the magnetic quantum anomalous Hall realization, which is a different step. I propose Kane and Molenkamp as the cleanest pair, accepting that other theory contributors (Mele, Bernevig, Zhang, Fu) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many independent experiments, including ARPES on three-dimensional materials. Mature and long discussed.
uncertainties: The credit list omits several decisive theorists, and the 2D and 3D parts could be recognised differently.
A narrow two-person split risks leaving out well-known co-originators.
Priority claims are from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong light-matter coupling with engineered artificial atoms routine and underlies superconducting quantum processors and readout. The work is original and has had large impact on quantum technology and quantum optics.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical proposal (Blais, Girvin and collaborators) and the first strong-coupling demonstration (Wallraff and Schoelkopf) are well identified. With four credited names, a three-person selection forces a choice between theory and experiment. I select the two experimentalists and Girvin as the theory anchor.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent confirmation. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits is adjacent, so the committee would have to weigh closeness to a very recent award.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent 2025 prize for superconducting circuit quantum effects.
The choice between Blais and Girvin on the theory side is not obvious from the supplied credit.
Whether the discovery is better seen as a technology platform than a single physical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spin-orbit torques allow electrical switching of magnetisation without spin-polarised injection, linking spin Hall and interfacial Rashba physics to magnetic memory. The topic is squarely within magnetism and spin dynamics and has practical impact on MRAM.
assessment.attribution: Miron and Gambardella showed switching by in-plane current in Pt/Co/AlOx, and Buhrman's group demonstrated spin-Hall torque switching. Theoretical and earlier spin Hall contributors are not in the supplied credit, and the origin of the torques is shared between spin Hall and interfacial mechanisms, so the allocation is somewhat contested.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of confirmation, with commercial development under way. The microscopic decomposition of the torques is still being refined, so it is somewhat early.
uncertainties: The relative roles of bulk spin Hall and interfacial Rashba-Edelstein effects are still debated.
Several theorists and experimental groups with decisive roles are not in the credit.
Possibly better to wait for further technology maturity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third class of collinear magnetic order with compensated moments but spin-split bands, which was found through symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations and then seen in spectroscopy. Conceptually clean and highly relevant to the magnetism community, with spintronic promise.
assessment.attribution: Smejkal, Jungwirth and Sinova are the central group. Earlier related ideas on spin-split antiferromagnets from other authors (for example Yuan, Hayami and collaborators) are not in the supplied credit, so priority is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation by ARPES and related probes has appeared, but only within the last few years, so it is early. I rank it here as promising rather than ready.
uncertainties: Maturity is limited, with the strength of independent confirmations still growing.
Priority relative to earlier spin-split antiferromagnet work is partly unresolved.
Device impact is not yet demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmion lattices in chiral magnets showed topological spin textures with emergent electrodynamics, and they connect to my own work on spin textures and atomistic spin dynamics. The ideas are original and have spawned a large field. Applications remain largely prospective.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit has only two names. Pfleiderer's group (with Muhlbauer and colleagues, in MnSi) and Tokura's group (real-space imaging in FeCoSi) are both decisive. The theoretical prediction (Bogdanov and others) is not in the credit, so the configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Well reproduced across materials and imaging methods. Practical device impact has been slower than anticipated, which makes the timing less compelling than for more established candidates.
uncertainties: The theoretical prediction by Bogdanov and colleagues falls outside the supplied credit.
Technological payoff is not yet realised.
Several other experimental contributors may have claims.
